newsitem.title: CANADA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-FLYERS WIN BUT COFFEY KNOCKED OUT BY TEAMMATE LINDROS.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-FLYERS WIN BUT COFFEY KNOCKED OUT BY TEAMMATE LINDROS.

text.p: Eric Lindros knocked teammate Paul Coffey out in the first period, then helped the Philadelphia Flyers knock out the Vancouver Canucks 5-3 by starting a four-goal outburst in the third.

Lindros tied the game 2-2 on the power play 1:09 into the third period. John LeClair and Mikael Renberg then scored in a 2:15 span and Joel Otto scored shorthanded with 3:23 to go as the Flyers extended their unbeaten streak to 14 games.
Coffey collided with Lindros with 6:32 left in the first.

The veteran defenceman lay motionless on the ice for over five minutes, then was carried off the ice on a stretcher and taken to a local hospital after the game. Coffey was expected to remain there overnight for observation.
"I'm a little dizzy, lightheaded and have a sore neck with a big welt on the back of my head," said Coffey. "But other than that, I feel great."

He added: "I definitely didn't see him (Lindros), I just remember Janne (Niinimaa) with the puck and I was going up the middle. He didn't give it to me, so I turned to go up the ice and I don't remember anything else."

"I was still in shock after what occurred in the first period," said Lindros. "I was in a funk all day. The guys are really concerned about how Paul is and we went to see him after the first and second periods and thank God he's all right. I don't want to remember that."
Philadelphia is 12-0-2 during its unbeaten streak and took sole possession of first place in the Atlantic Division, moving two points ahead of idle Florida.

In Tampa, Rick Tabaracci made 25 saves and Chris Gratton and Alexander Selivanov scored 45 seconds apart in the first period as the Lightning snapped a six-game winless streak with a 4-2 victory over the New York Rangers.
John Cullen and Roman Hamrlik also scored for the Lightning, who had not won since December 16 but beat the Rangers for the third time in as many games this season.
Tabaracci stopped 24 of the first 25 shots he faced until Brian Noonan scored with 93 seconds to go, pulling the Rangers within 3-2.

Glenn Healy stopped 28 shots for the Rangers, who finished 10-3-1 in December. Healy fell to 2-7-3 in place of starting goalie Mike Richter, who has a personal unbeaten streak of 13 games (12-0-1) but was rested after playing seven of the last eight games.
In Buffalo, Alexei Zhitnik had a goal and an assist and six different players scored goals as the Sabres hung on for a 6-5 victory over the New Jersey Devils.
The game was a contrast with the teams' meeting eight days ago, when the teams skated to a scoreless tie and Sabres goaltender Dominik Hasek and New Jersey backstop Martin Brodeur each made 37 saves.
In the rematch, Buffalo chased Brodeur by scoring three goals on six shots in the first period.

Bill Guerin recorded his first career hat trick for the Devils, who almost erased a 6-2 deficit in the final 8:35. Guerin and Dave Andreychuk scored 26 seconds apart to make it 6-5 with 1:39 to play, but Hasek, who made 31 saves, stopped five shots to blunt a final New Jersey flurry.
In Calgary, Ulf Dahlen scored twice in a four-goal third period and Chris Terreri made 29 saves as the San Jose Sharks routed the Flames 5-1 in a Pacific Division matchup.
Jeff Friesen scored once and assisted on three goals for San Jose, which won for just the fifth time in its last 15 games in Calgary.
The Sharks were without defenceman Greg Hawgood, who was suspended for two games by the NHL as a result of a slashing incident against Edmonton defenceman Boris Mironov in a game last Saturday.

Ed Ward scored the lone goal of the game for Calgary, with assists from Dale McTavish and Sami Helenius. All three were called up from the minors earlier in the day by the Flames, who are 1-5-1 in their last seven games.
In Chicago, Adam Deadmarsh scored twice and Joe Sakic added three assists as the Colorado Avalanche buried the Blackhawks 4-1.
Sandis Ozolinsh and Keith Jones broke open a 1-1 second-period tie with a pair of power-play tallies.
Both Colorado and Philadelphia have 51 points, best in the NHL.
